text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pregnant women's rights affirmed: Manitoba court cites freedom to indulge in harmful habits despite risk to fetus.
- Miners get set for staking marathon: Vast Ontario tract to open Tuesday.
- Ontario to build super prisons: 'No frills' facilities will house 2,200.
- Francophones test lower in literacy levels: Difference from anglophone results may be rooted in Canada's past, analysts say.
- Jailed Canadian a 'pawn' in RCMP sting: Agents tricked man into setting up Thai herion buy, former member of watchdog panel says.
- Toronto Stock Exchange targets First Marathon Securities Ltd: Two top executives to appear at hearing on charges of improper supervision of accounts.
- Royal Bank of Canada buyback tops C$1-billion: Bank aims for 10 percent of its shares.
- Huge IMF gold sale in works: Move to ease poor nations' debts could depress metal's price.
- Hydro-Quebec pursues Gaz Metropolitain CEO: Andre Caille touted as Premier's pick.
- Stock debacles spur probe: Brokerage industry goes under the regulatory microscope in aftershock of Cartaway and Timbuktu disasters. First Marathon says it did nothing wrong.
- Royal Bank to spend C$1 billion to buy back shares.
